notes: The frontend is impressively polished for a single-file app: clear three-column layout with facets/results/breakdown, well-designed error state with caret positioning, score breakdown cards, and consistent color system with proper type hierarchy. The backend demonstrates genuine index design (inverted indexes, n-gram title index, sorted numeric arrays with bisect) and smart top-k scoring via heapq.nsmallest. However, the single-file monolith hurts readability and extensibility significantly — ~1000 lines mixing lexer, parser, engine, HTTP, and an enormous HTML string literal would be daunting for a new engineer. The LRU-style cache eviction (delete first N keys from dict) is simplistic and could evict hot entries. The _collect method has a subtle bug with `stack.append and stack.pop()` that works by accident (append returns None, so it always evaluates pop). Thread safety relies on an RLock but eval/score_set read indexes without holding it.
